set.approach: The wall is a bolted, north-facing drytool crag along the western end of the Devil's Castle north face, in a boxy recess above the main rock-climbing area and before the base of the Hellevator Shaft. From the upper parking area by the campground (or on foot from the Alta base), walk through the campground and past the cabins onto the Devil's Castle loop trail, and leave it at a bend where small mine tailings sit beside the path. A climbers' trail climbs talus to the foot of the castle, then trends right past the standard rock routes and up loose scree to the recess holding the wall. The rock below is loose, so wear a helmet. Sloth is the leftmost line on the wall.

review.notes: Wall/approach from the 7even area page and the parent drytool area page (one lineage). Position from the route page. Descent only where the page says lower.

set.approach: The route climbs the big chimney at the left-hand end of the Devil's Castle north face. In winter and spring the way in is on skis from the Alta base area, through avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast and judge snow stability on the way to the base. The line starts a few feet right of the chimney and traverses left into it.

review.notes: Route page for location and start; parent area page for the winter approach. No descent stated (finishing options only), so none written. Route page lists a rock grade; the repeat described M-grades.

set.approach: Start from the Middle Fork of the Weber River trailhead at the end of the Weber Canyon road and follow the Middle Fork trail up the valley to the sign for the Abes Lake turnoff. Continue a short way past the sign to a clearing on the right, then leave the trail and head west uphill, passing through a small notch and picking the easiest line up to Adax Lake. The flows hang from the band of cliffs on the west side, higher than the lake and its meadow. Serenity is the main flow, north of the lake.

review.notes: Approach from the Adax Zone and parent area pages; no descent stated. Numbers omitted: single page.

set.approach: Park at the Pine Hollow trailhead, walk up the road to the north Timpanogos trailhead and follow the trail until the ice comes into view across the canyon. Work down into the gully and climb it to the base of the flow. The slopes around it carry avalanche danger, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Build a V-thread at the top and rappel the route.

review.notes: Single route page; distances omitted.

set.approach: Going up American Fork Canyon from the guard shack, the pillar is the first obvious ice feature, on your right. Park at the next turnout, cross the creek, and climb the thin ice slabs to the foot of the steep pillar.
set.descent_text: Walk to the trees above and left of the pillar and rappel the route; bolted anchors on the west side serve as rappel stations, and the tat on them should be replaced.

review.notes: Single route page; rappel length omitted.

set.approach: The north side of the American Fork Twins is reached through Gad Valley above Little Cottonwood Canyon; park by the bridge near the Tram base. The north aspect lies inside the ski area, so check the area's access rules before going, and check the avalanche forecast. The flow sits high in the middle bowl of the north face, climber's right of the large Pipeline couloir that drops from the West Twin summit.
set.descent_text: If you continue up the Center Chute above the flow, you reach the small saddle between the two Twins. From there, walk east along the crest onto the East Twin and drop north down its ridge toward Hidden Peak.

review.notes: Route page for location and descent; Saved by the Turf page agrees the ridge east of the Center Chute descends toward Hidden Peak. Descent applies to the Center Chute continuation, as the page states.

set.approach: The line begins in a large chimney weakness left of The Rookie Party and left of Pipeline. From the top of Hidden Peak, descend the ski run called Road to Provo and traverse around a short sub-ridge of the Twins to reach the start. The north aspect is ski-area terrain, so check access rules and the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: After the rope pitches the route joins the Center Chute and finishes on the ridge. The way off is the east ridge, which is fourth-class ground leading back to Hidden Peak.

review.notes: Route page; descent direction toward Hidden Peak corroborated by Rookie Party page.

set.approach: The north side of the American Fork Twins is reached through Gad Valley above Little Cottonwood Canyon; park by the bridge near the Tram base. The north aspect lies inside the ski area, so check the area's access rules before going, and check the avalanche forecast. The Hooker Party is on the northwest face, around the rib from Pipeline, high up below the saddle with Red Top.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: The north side of the American Fork Twins is reached through Gad Valley above Little Cottonwood Canyon; park by the bridge near the Tram base. The north aspect lies inside the ski area, so check the area's access rules before going, and check the avalanche forecast. Veteran Obsession is two short flows on the northwest face, down and left of The Hooker Party, reached by climbing a small snowfield to the first step.
set.descent_text: The route is short and parties walk off after the upper step.

review.notes: Walk-off stated on route page.

set.descent_text: Belay from a tree at the top and walk off.

review.notes: Location only 'below AF twins', so no approach written.

set.descent_text: The line is a series of low-angle ice blobs, and parties walk off.

review.notes: Route page gives no location; approach skipped. Walk-off stated.

set.approach: Drive up Big Cottonwood Canyon to the Mill B parking area and take the Broads Fork trail south to the beaver pond, where you enter the cirque. The flows form across the lower cliff band beneath the Twins.
set.descent_text: Plan on V-threads; there is little in the rock for rappel anchors.

review.notes: Route page for the V-thread descent; area page for the approach. Stored coordinate (40.5276,-111.7241) sits near Hogum Fork / Lone Peak, not Broads Fork; MP carries the same coordinate.

set.approach: Follow the forest road to the Duchesne Tunnel. The ice begins right by a little concrete diversion structure where the tunnel starts.
set.descent_text: A bolted anchor high on climber's right serves for rappelling or lowering. You can also walk down, or continue up the gorge over several small headwalls and climb out to the road at the top.

review.notes: Route page and area page agree on a bolted anchor at climber's right. No numbers.

set.approach: Drive up the Duchesne River valley on the East Portal road to the Duchesne River diversion dam. Before the dam, turn north onto an ATV track and follow it to a primitive trailhead where it ends. Take the trail north, then climb a boulderfield to the base of the climb.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the large pine on climber's left, a free-hanging drop that lands back at the base. Anchors at the top are natural; be wary of loose rock on the top-outs.

review.notes: Single route page; distances omitted.

set.approach: Drive up the Duchesne River valley on the East Portal road to the Duchesne River diversion dam. Before the dam, turn north onto an ATV track and follow it to a primitive trailhead. Hike the trail north to a place where you can cross the gorge, then climb up Marsell Canyon Creek until the ice steepens.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: Drive up the Duchesne River valley on the East Portal road to the Duchesne River diversion dam. Above the dam, climb the peak's west side by the easiest line, trending to climber's right through a cliff band to reach easier ground. The line lies left within the prominent gully on that peak and is visible once you are up there. It is a long, steep approach.

review.notes: No descent stated; elevations omitted.

set.approach: The falls are the middle of three drainages across from Cobblerest Campground on the Mirror Lake Highway. Thrash across to the drainage and use a faint path up the streambed, which may be dry; ice may not appear until the last boulders below the climb.
set.descent_text: Walk off to climber's left, or V-thread or top-rope from the flow. Bolted anchors sit above the last step on the right.

review.notes: Single route page.

set.approach: Park at the pullout with a yellow curve warning sign a little way up the road from Cobblerest Campground, ford the river and go up the clear stream channel to the ice. It can also be reached by traversing north from Hard to Find Falls.
set.descent_text: Both pitches have rappel rings on their anchors (a boulder with webbing at the top of the first, pins with cord at the second).

review.notes: Single route page; distances omitted.

set.approach: Approach as for Hard to Find Falls, bushwhacking to the drainage across from Cobblerest Campground. Its bolts start to the right of the falls and join the upper curtain.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: Approach as for Hard to Find Falls, bushwhacking to the drainage across from Cobblerest Campground. The line is directly behind the falls, slightly right of centre.

review.notes: No descent stated (two-bolt anchor at top right only).

set.approach: The Mill Flat trail leaves from the Iron Mine and Hades campgrounds and runs up the North Fork of the Duchesne River. Crimson Column is a short, steep pillar on the right, just off the trail.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: The Mill Flat trail leaves from the Iron Mine and Hades campgrounds and runs up the North Fork of the Duchesne River. Follow it to the ice high on the red cliff above the first line of trees, before Gallery of Glass. The best access is a large red rock wash that leads to the base, with a steep hillside and talus above the trail.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: The Mill Flat trail leaves from the Iron Mine and Hades campgrounds and runs up the North Fork of the Duchesne River. Gallery of Glass is on the right, past an area of deadfall.

review.notes: No descent stated.

set.approach: The climb is high on the left side of the valley in the east-facing lower red cliff bands, after a steep hillside and talus. One way is to cross the river directly from the parking area, climb a series of benches, then traverse right until the lower band of red cliffs shows the climb. The other is to go a short way up the North Fork and begin a rising traverse right across the benches, looking for easy clefts through the short cliff bands.
set.descent_text: Descend by a thread drilled into the ice at the top of the flow. The big pine above is not worth using, since the rope tends to jam.

review.notes: Single route page.

set.approach: The Mill Flat trail leaves from the Iron Mine and Hades campgrounds and runs up the North Fork of the Duchesne River. Walk up it, then turn right onto a subtle ridge dividing two talus fields and climb steeply to the base. The flow is visible from the trail by looking up through the trees to the ridge top after passing the Slate Creek drainage.

review.notes: No descent stated; distances omitted.

set.approach: Start from the Y couloir trailhead lot, at the mouth of the Hogum Fork canyon. Cross the creek and climb the bushy and talus slopes below the Z gullies. Z Left is the leftmost of three long Z gullies that form early in winter, left of the Y couloir, so cut left across the slope to it.
set.descent_text: Rappel from trees and V-threads; long ropes help. Carry cord for rappel anchors.

review.notes: Single route page.

set.approach: Start from the Y couloir trailhead lot, at the mouth of the Hogum Fork canyon. Cross the creek and climb the bushy and talus slopes below the Z gullies. Z Center is the middle of three long Z gullies that form early in winter, left of the Y couloir.

review.notes: Descent not stated.

set.approach: Leave the car opposite the Lisa Falls lot, follow the path down to the creek and cross it. Angle up and left to a gully and follow that to the foot of the route.

review.notes: Single route page.

set.approach: Use the same approach as the Z gullies and the Y couloir. The route is in the cliffs left of and below the Y couloir; find the grove of green pines under the first big bend of the couloir, and the route is directly below it, well to climber's right of the rightmost Z gully. Skis or snowshoes help in deep snow, and the couloir above is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: No descent stated (V-thread material mentioned only as a precaution).
